texto.@es: Para un plan futuro ya organizado, usa sujeto + am/is/are + verbo-ing, a menudo con una hora o fecha: **I'm meeting Lucy at five** (he quedado con Lucy a las cinco). El contexto temporal indica que no está ocurriendo ahora.
texto.@en: For a future plan already organized, use subject + am / is / are + verbo-ing, often with an hour or date: **I'm meeting Lucy at five** (I have met Lucy at 5: 00). The time context indicates that it is not happening now.

titulo.@en: This is a continuous and going to

texto.@es: **Be going to + verbo base** suele destacar un plan o intención ya decididos: **We're going to visit Spain this year** (vamos a visitar España este año). Los usos pueden solaparse; el presente continuo suele presentar un acuerdo más concreto. Es una tendencia, no una regla absoluta.
texto.@en: **Be going to + verbo base** usually highlights an already decided plan or intention: **We're going to visit Spain this year** (we will visit Spain this year). The uses may overlap; the continuous present often presents a more specific agreement. It's a trend, not an absolute rule.

texto.@es: Para un horario fijo, como el de un transporte, es común el presente simple: **The plane leaves at ten** (el avión sale a las diez). Una persona también puede decir **I'm leaving at ten** para contar su propio plan.
texto.@en: For a fixed time, such as a transport, the simple present is common: **The plane leaves at ten** (the plane leaves at 10: 00). A person can also say **I'm leaving at ten** to tell his own plan.
